decision.rationale: All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have phenotype-aligned endpoints (all report abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA but still aligned). The strongest directly PRS-comparable performance evidence in the metadata is for PGS001784, which reports a PRS-only Nagelkerke R² (covariates regressed out) of 0.014661 in Europeans; other candidates either report only full-model discrimination (e.g., AUROC/C-index) or non-R² metrics (e.g., partial-r) without an explicit PRS-only AUC/R². However, the overall evidence remains limited/partly non-comparable across the set: several models lack PRS-only metrics entirely, and some reported high full-model metrics (e.g., C-index 0.882 for PGS003973) are likely covariate-driven and not directly comparable to PRS-only performance. Therefore a direct-match exists but the best choice is supported only moderately well from the visible metadata.

decision.rationale: All four candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target alcohol dependence via alcohol use disorder / alcohol dependence measurement. PGS002738 is the most endpoint-faithful (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both explicitly alcohol use disorder; trait_efo = alcohol dependence) and provides the strongest visible discrimination evidence among the set via an OR(top 10% vs rest)=1.96 (95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a European evaluation sample (n=7,900), which is more directly interpretable for case/control risk stratification than the two problematic-alcohol-use models that only report small ΔR² values (0.01192 and 0.00456) on a DSM-5 criteria count outcome. However, confidence is limited because none of the candidates report PRS-only AUC/R², covariates are unknown for PGS002738 (reducing comparability), and PGS000201 has a similar EUR validation size with cleaner disclosed covariates but a less direct (quantitative criteria-count) endpoint and weaker incremental-metric evidence.
